text: TES Component Design and Manufacturing (Milestone 1.3 & 1.5) Design Criteria The thermal battery design was conducted considering the following criteria: • Heat exchanger performance: the TES exchanges heat between water and the PCM material through a secondary loop. The required design target is 14-17 kW for 2 hours. The extra capacity includes the compressor power during cooling discharge mode. • Weight: especially for packaged RTUs, weight is a constraint. Designing a lighter TES will be necessary; thus, reducing the weight of either the heat exchanger or the PCM should be considered. • Material compatibility: Corrosion tests were conducted for uncoated and coated aluminum alloy specimens • TES cost: aluminum off-the-shelf HXs were a good option to bring down the cost. Furthermore, off-the-shelf bins were used to reduce overall manufacturing costs, rather than having a custom-built TES tank. Page 25 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park Corrosion Testing Given the corrosive nature of salt hydrate PCMs, HX material samples from several research partners were analyzed for material corrosion. To test for corrosion, the HX samples were immersed in the selected PCM for 3 months. The HX samples were: 1. Base aluminum HX samples (Figure 16) 2. Wire HX, coated with black epoxy (Figure 17). This HX configuration is common on older refrigerators as a condenser, lying flat on the back of the unit. 3. Plate-type HX coated with white epoxy (Figure 18) Figure 16: The Rheem HX sample a) Immersed and b) control (non-immersed) Figure 17: Wire HX, coated with black epoxy, a) Immersed and b) control (non-immersed) Page 26 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park Figure 18: Plate-type HX coated with white epoxy a) Immersed and b) control (non-immersed) Using a Nikon 35X Stereo-zoom microscope with AM scope 16MP camera system and measurement system, each sample was monitored for: (i) coating layer thickness degradation, (ii) pitting cracks, and (iii) any corrosive effects. For the first HX sample, bare aluminum HX, the results indicate that the HX section corroded. Figure 19a at 10x magnification showed surface corrosion. Under 20x magnification, small holes can be seen (pointed by the red arrows). These are localized pitting holes. It is interesting to note that some areas of the tube are highly corroded, as shown, but other areas are not. However, even if only some areas of the tube are corroded, bare tubes are not safe to use (Figure 19b). Figure 19: Microscopic camera photos of the bare aluminum HX surfaces for a) immersed at 10x magnification, b) immersed at 20x magnification, and c) the control sample For the wire HX, coated with black epoxy, the control sample was magnified and showed no corrosion (Figure 20a). At 20x, the immersed part shows visible corrosion near the wires-to-tube location (Figure 20b). The plate-type HX coated with white epoxy showed no corrosion effects at all, so it seems impervious to the salt hydrate PCM (Figure 18).
